answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks via radio time-of-flight localization. Each node emits an ultra-wideband signal to receivers along a transit bridge anchored in basalt bedrock, proving its unique physical position. Faking identities requires deploying separate transmitters at distinct coordinates, imposing real hardware and deployment costs on an attacker per node. However, multipath reflections from steel trusses distort timing accuracy, occasionally causing false rejections.
